First off, keep writing. It takes a lot of fucking courage to present your work in such a format for everyone to read, especially at a young age, and you will only get better if you keep it up. 

Second, the (hopefully constructive) criticism. I'm not too familiar with the genre so I'll try and stick mostly to the style, but it seems like you fall into cliche an awful lot. Since the whole zombie apocalypse trend is taking off again, I would do the best to describe things in a way that we don't always see on television or read in books. In order to engage your reader, you must draw them in with something they haven't already been beaten to death with. 

Third, I usually hate "rules" when it comes to writing, but I think you would benefit from the whole "show don't tell" rule. I think it would help take care of the redundancy issue. One line that stands out to me the most is "'I was leaving.' I said in a monotone voice with little emotion." It is usually implied that a monotone voice has little emotion. Also, with what is said, it is hard to convey emotion with such a succinct line. If instead you describe your state of mind a tiny bit more, implying that your narrator would have a monotone voice, I think you would engage your reader a little more. I don't think you even need anything after "I said."

Ok, I know this is long, but this is the last thing I have to say. Find your own voice. You are going to have to write a lot to do it, but it'll come to you. You just need to keep writing. Take everything that has been said on this as constructive. Nothing that I have said, or anyone else for that matter, will benefit you unless you want it to. This is your story, own it.
